question: A 28-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 6-month history of progressive fatigue and intermittent diarrhea. During this time, he has had a 6-kg (13-lb) weight loss. Physical examination shows pale conjunctivae. Abdominal examination shows tenderness to palpation in the lower quadrants. An image from a colonoscopy of the descending colon is shown. Further evaluation is most likely to show which of the following findings?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Chronic diarrhea and weight loss -> Malabsorption -> Nutritional deficiency -> Anemia -> Pale conjunctivae -> Iron deficiency anemia -> 80% CHAIN: Abdominal tenderness -> Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) -> Colonoscopy findings -> Descending colon involvement -> Further evaluation for IBD markers -> Anti-Saccharomyces cerevisiae antibodies -> 75% CHAIN: Chronic diarrhea and weight loss -> Malabsorption -> Celiac disease suspicion -> Further evaluation -> Anti-tissue transglutaminase antibodies -> 80%
analysis: The patient's presentation with fatigue, weight loss, diarrhea, and pale conjunctivae suggests a malabsorption syndrome. The image from colonoscopy showing changes in the descending colon is indicative of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Given the clinical scenario, further evaluation is most likely to show the presence of anti-Saccharomyces cerevisiae antibodies (ASCA), which are associated with Crohn's disease, a type of IBD.
